cards.front: What are the main steps in the formation of an atherosclerotic plaque?
cards.back: **Endothelial injury** lets LDL enter the intima, where it is **oxidized**. Macrophages take it up and become **foam cells** (**fatty streak**). **PDGF** brings **smooth muscle cells** from the media; they form a **fibrous cap** over a necrotic lipid core.
cards.back_pt: A **lesão endotelial** permite a entrada do LDL na íntima, onde ele é **oxidado**. Macrófagos o captam e se tornam **células espumosas** (**estria gordurosa**). O **PDGF** atrai **células musculares lisas** da camada média; elas formam uma **capa fibrosa** sobre um núcleo lipídico necrótico.

cards.front: Which arteries are most often affected by atherosclerosis?
cards.back: From most to least common: **abdominal aorta** > **coronary arteries** > **popliteal arteries** > **internal carotid arteries** > circle of Willis. Plaques form mainly at **branch points**, where blood flow is turbulent.
cards.back_pt: Do mais para o menos comum: **aorta abdominal** > **artérias coronárias** > **artérias poplíteas** > **artérias carótidas internas** > polígono de Willis. As placas se formam principalmente em **bifurcações**, onde o fluxo sanguíneo é turbulento.

cards.front: Why is CK-MB useful to detect reinfarction a few days after an MI?
cards.back: **Troponin I or T** is the most sensitive and specific marker, but it stays high for about **7-10 days**. **CK-MB** returns to normal within about **2-3 days**, so a new rise in CK-MB suggests **reinfarction**.
cards.back_pt: A **troponina I ou T** é o marcador mais sensível e específico, mas permanece elevada por cerca de **7-10 dias**. A **CK-MB** volta ao normal em cerca de **2-3 dias**, então uma nova elevação da CK-MB sugere **reinfarto**.

cards.front: What is the usual microscopic timeline after a myocardial infarction?
cards.back: **4-24 h**: early **coagulative necrosis** (wavy fibers). **1-3 days**: **neutrophils**. **3-7 days**: **macrophages** remove dead myocytes. **1-2 weeks**: **granulation tissue** from the margins. **2 weeks to 2 months**: collagen deposition and a **scar**.
cards.back_pt: **4-24 h**: início da **necrose de coagulação** (fibras onduladas). **1-3 dias**: **neutrófilos**. **3-7 dias**: **macrófagos** removem os miócitos mortos. **1-2 semanas**: **tecido de granulação** a partir das margens. **2 semanas a 2 meses**: deposição de colágeno e **cicatriz**.

cards.front: Why are myocardial ruptures most likely about 3-14 days after an MI?
cards.back: **Macrophages** clear dead tissue before **granulation tissue** and collagen make the wall strong, so the infarct is **softest** then. Ruptures: **free wall** (tamponade), **interventricular septum** (left-to-right shunt), **papillary muscle** (acute mitral regurgitation).
cards.back_pt: Os **macrófagos** removem o tecido morto antes que o **tecido de granulação** e o colágeno fortaleçam a parede, então o infarto está **mais frágil** nessa fase. Rupturas: **parede livre** (tamponamento cardíaco), **septo interventricular** (shunt esquerda-direita), **músculo papilar** (insuficiência mitral aguda).

cards.front: How does early post-MI pericarditis differ from Dressler syndrome?
cards.back: **Early pericarditis** (1-3 days): **fibrinous** inflammation over a **transmural** infarct; pleuritic pain and a friction rub. **Dressler syndrome** (weeks later): **autoimmune** pericarditis against myocardial antigens released by necrosis; fever, pleuritic pain, friction rub.
cards.back_pt: **Pericardite precoce** (1-3 dias): inflamação **fibrinosa** sobre um infarto **transmural**; dor pleurítica e atrito pericárdico. **Síndrome de Dressler** (semanas depois): pericardite **autoimune** contra antígenos miocárdicos liberados pela necrose; febre, dor pleurítica, atrito pericárdico.

cards.front: What is a true left ventricular aneurysm after an MI, and what are its risks?
cards.back: A thin, **dyskinetic** bulge of **scar** tissue that forms weeks to months after a large (often anterior) MI. The ECG may show **persistent ST elevation**. Risks: **mural thrombus** with embolism, heart failure and arrhythmias. It rarely ruptures.
cards.back_pt: Um abaulamento **discinético** de parede fina, formado por tecido **cicatricial**, que surge semanas a meses após um IAM extenso (geralmente anterior). O ECG pode mostrar **supradesnivelamento persistente do segmento ST**. Riscos: **trombo mural** com embolia, insuficiência cardíaca e arritmias. Raramente se rompe.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old man is admitted with an anterior STEMI. He arrived 14 hours after the pain started and did not receive reperfusion. Two days after the pain started, he has a cardiac arrest on the ward and cannot be resuscitated. At autopsy, the anterior wall of the left ventricle shows a poorly defined, mottled area. Which microscopic finding is most likely in this area?
choices: Wavy myocardial fibers with no inflammatory cells
Macrophages filled with debris from dead myocytes
Coagulative necrosis with a dense infiltrate of neutrophils
Granulation tissue with new capillaries and fibroblasts
Dense collagen scar with few cells
questions.explanation: At **1-3 days** after an MI, the dead myocytes show **coagulative necrosis**, and **neutrophils** fill the area. Macrophages become the main cells at about **3-7 days**, so they are the tempting but later finding. Wavy fibers without inflammation fit the first hours, granulation tissue fits 1-2 weeks, and a collagen scar fits weeks to months.
questions.explanation_pt: Entre **1 e 3 dias** após o IAM, os miócitos mortos mostram **necrose de coagulação** e **neutrófilos** infiltram a área. Os macrófagos passam a predominar por volta de **3-7 dias**, por isso são a alternativa tentadora, mas correspondem a uma fase posterior. Fibras onduladas sem inflamação são das primeiras horas, tecido de granulação de 1-2 semanas e cicatriz de colágeno de semanas a meses.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman is in the hospital 4 days after an inferior STEMI. She suddenly develops severe shortness of breath. Blood pressure is 84/50 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. There is a new holosystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla, and crackles over both lungs. Chest x-ray shows pulmonary edema. Which complication is most likely?
choices: Rupture of the posteromedial papillary muscle
Rupture of the left ventricular free wall
questions.explanation: Sudden **acute mitral regurgitation** (apical holosystolic murmur to the axilla, pulmonary edema, shock) a few days after an MI suggests **papillary muscle rupture**. The **posteromedial** papillary muscle usually has a single blood supply (the posterior descending artery), so it is the one at risk in inferior MI. Septal rupture also causes a new holosystolic murmur and can cause pulmonary congestion, but the murmur is loudest at the lower **left sternal border**, often with a thrill, and the key finding is a left-to-right shunt (higher oxygen saturation in the right ventricle than in the right atrium). Free-wall rupture causes tamponade, not a new murmur.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma **insuficiência mitral aguda** súbita (sopro holossistólico apical irradiando para a axila, edema pulmonar, choque) poucos dias após o IAM sugere **ruptura de músculo papilar**. O músculo papilar **posteromedial** geralmente tem irrigação única (artéria descendente posterior), por isso é o vulnerável no IAM inferior. A ruptura do septo também causa um novo sopro holossistólico e pode causar congestão pulmonar, mas o sopro é mais audível na **borda esternal esquerda** baixa, muitas vezes com frêmito, e o achado-chave é um shunt esquerda-direita (saturação de O2 maior no ventrículo direito do que no átrio direito). A ruptura de parede livre causa tamponamento, não um novo sopro.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman who smokes has had several episodes of chest pain over the past month. The episodes happen at rest, usually around 5 AM, and last about 10 minutes. They do not happen with exercise. An ECG during one episode shows ST elevation in leads V2-V4 that returns to baseline within 15 minutes. Serial troponin levels are normal. Coronary angiography shows no significant stenosis. Which mechanism best explains her symptoms?
choices: Plaque rupture with a partly occlusive thrombus
Fixed coronary stenosis that limits flow during exertion
Oxygen demand exceeding supply in a hypertrophied ventricle
Transient spasm of an epicardial coronary artery
questions.explanation: Chest pain at rest, often early in the morning, with **transient ST elevation**, normal troponin and no significant stenosis is **Prinzmetal (vasospastic) angina**. **Smoking** is a key risk factor; cocaine and triptans can also trigger spasm. Unstable angina also occurs at rest, but it comes from **plaque rupture** with a partly occlusive thrombus, so angiography shows a culprit lesion; its ECG is often normal or shows ST depression or T-wave inversion. Calcium channel blockers and nitrates relieve the spasm.
questions.explanation_pt: Dor torácica em repouso, geralmente de madrugada, com **supradesnivelamento transitório do ST**, troponina normal e ausência de estenose significativa é **angina de Prinzmetal (vasoespástica)**. O **tabagismo** é um fator de risco importante; cocaína e triptanos também podem desencadear o espasmo. A angina instável também ocorre em repouso, mas resulta de **ruptura de placa** com trombo parcialmente oclusivo, então a coronariografia mostra uma lesão culpada; o ECG costuma ser normal ou mostrar infradesnivelamento do ST ou inversão de onda T. Bloqueadores dos canais de cálcio e nitratos aliviam o espasmo.
